newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - FX vols edge up on dollar weakness.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - FX vols edge up on dollar weakness.

text.p: Implied volatility levels for dollar/mark options garnered support Monday from the spot's break below 1.7000 marks, but remained at relatively low levels, options analysts said.

One-month dollar/mark volatility gained 0.4 point, rising to 8.70/9.00 percent versus Friday's levels this morning, as the market began to anticipate dollar/mark would breach key price support at 1.7000, analysts said. The dollar was recently bid at 1.6965 marks after its first dip below 1.7000 in two weeks.
"Market makers are getting a little bit more concerned about the risk here" as dollar/mark explores the downside, said an options trader for a U.S. bank on the West Coast.
One-month dollar/mark volatility has since edged back to 8.65/8.95 percent. One-year volatility remained essentially flat at 9.05/9.25 percent.

The mark strengthened this morning on fresh European monetary union jitters related to French President Jacques Chirac's call for an early parliamentary election and to concern about Italy's ability to meet EMU criteria.
In the options market, a one-billion-mark sale of two-week mark calls/franc puts in the 3.375 strike was observed.

Short-term dollar/mark risk reversals shifted to favor mark calls, underscoring the market's downside bias for the dollar, while on European crosses, one-month 25-delta mark/franc and mark/lira risk reversals also were bid for the mark, the West Coast trader said.
One-month 25-delta dollar/mark risk reversals were skewed 0.05 to 0.35 for mark calls.
Dollar/yen risk reversals also remained skewed to yen calls after moving away from a yen put bias last week. The one-month risk reversal was 0.10 to 0.50 favoring mark calls.
Implied volatilities for one-month dollar/yen options also edged upward, to 8.80/9.10 percent from 8.40//8.70 Friday. One-year was steady at 9.85/10.05 percent.

Traders traced the uptick in dollar/yen volatility to general uncertainty before the Group of Seven finance ministers meet over the weekend. They noted market participants were squaring positions ahead of the event, lending a quiet tone to the market.

Dollar/yen remained rangebound in the spot market, holding above 125.00. One New York-based trader for a Japanese Bank said selling of dollar/yen straddles last week in 124.00 and 127.00 strikes set the market's near-term parameters.
